options.text: Deploy the IPS in monitor-only (detection) mode for the first month to analyse traffic patterns, tune the signature database, and gradually enable blocking rules for high-confidence threats.
Implement the IPS in full prevention mode immediately with a conservative, pre-configured rule set, establishing a rapid-response team to handle and resolve false positives in real time.
Segment the network and deploy the IPS in active prevention mode only on high-risk zones first, while keeping low-risk zones in detection-only mode as you refine the security policies.
Work with application owners to define strict traffic whitelists, then configure the IPS to block all non-conforming traffic at the perimeter, updating the rules weekly based on operational feedback.

what_worked_well: Minimises the risk of disrupting legitimate business traffic by allowing you to baseline normal network behaviour and tune rules.
trade_offs: Leaves the network temporarily vulnerable to active exploits during the monitoring phase, as the system will not block threats.
areas_to_consider: Ensure that the security team is actively monitoring alerts during this phase to respond manually to high-severity threats.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Tuning an IPS in detection mode is a standard industry practice to balance security posture with operational availability.

what_worked_well: Provides immediate protection against known threats from day one, significantly reducing the network's attack surface.
trade_offs: A conservative rule set might miss sophisticated attacks, while the rapid-response team may face high initial ticket volumes.
areas_to_consider: Establish clear escalation paths and playbooks for the rapid-response team to handle false positives efficiently.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Managing IPS policy enforcement requires a clear operational framework to mitigate the impact of false positives on business continuity.

what_worked_well: Focuses protection on the most critical assets first, reducing the overall risk profile while limiting the blast radius of false positives.
trade_offs: Managing different IPS policies across multiple network zones increases administrative complexity and configuration overhead.
areas_to_consider: Ensure that zone boundaries are clearly defined and that policy differences are well-documented to prevent security gaps.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Deploying IPS across segmented networks allows for granular security policies tailored to the risk profile of each zone.

what_worked_well: Establishes a highly secure, zero-trust approach at the perimeter, ensuring only explicitly permitted traffic is allowed.
trade_offs: Creating and maintaining comprehensive whitelists is extremely labour-intensive and can easily lead to accidental service outages.
areas_to_consider: Implement robust change management processes to ensure whitelists are updated dynamically as business services evolve.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Integrating whitelisting with IPS configurations requires deep visibility into application traffic patterns and business requirements.

question.situation: You are returning to work as a Computer Network Architect. The business wants to modernise its legacy office network to support a hybrid workforce. You need to present an initial high-level strategy to the stakeholders, but the existing network documentation is outdated.
question.task: How do you approach the initial phase of this redesign to ensure a robust foundation while managing stakeholder expectations?

options.text: Focus on active discovery using automated network mapping tools to establish an accurate baseline of the current infrastructure before proposing any architectural changes.
Propose a modern network architecture design based on industry standard templates first, then validate and adjust it against the physical environment during implementation.
Collaborate with the support and help desk teams to identify current pain points and user issues, using these insights to guide the initial design priorities.
Conduct a comprehensive manual audit of key network segments, updating the documentation manually while designing the new architecture in parallel.

hints: Consider how automated tools can save time when dealing with outdated legacy documentation.
Think about the balance between theoretical design standards and the actual physical constraints of the existing network.

what_worked_well: Using automated tools provides an objective, accurate, and rapid view of the active network topology.
trade_offs: Automated discovery might miss offline legacy segments or non-IP assets that require manual verification.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you have the necessary administrative credentials and security clearances to run discovery tools across all subnets.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Establishing an accurate baseline is critical for predicting how the new hybrid architecture will perform.

what_worked_well: Presenting a modern, standard-based design early helps stakeholders visualise the end-state and aligns with modern hybrid working trends.
trade_offs: Designing without a verified baseline risks creating a theoretical plan that is incompatible with legacy hardware constraints.
areas_to_consider: Be prepared to adapt the design significantly once the physical reality of the legacy network is uncovered.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding modern architectural frameworks ensures your proposed solution is scalable and secure.

what_worked_well: Engaging with front-line support teams ensures the new design directly addresses real-world user frustrations and operational issues.
trade_offs: This approach focuses heavily on subjective user experience and might overlook underlying structural network limitations.
areas_to_consider: Combine these user insights with technical telemetry to get a complete picture of the network's health.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Leveraging help desk data helps align technical network changes with actual business productivity needs.

what_worked_well: A manual audit combined with parallel design work keeps the project moving forward while ensuring deep familiarity with the physical infrastructure.
trade_offs: This is highly time-consuming and may delay the presentation of the high-level strategy to stakeholders.
areas_to_consider: Assess whether your return-to-work timeline allows for extensive manual documentation before delivery milestones.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Refining your mapping skills helps streamline the transition from legacy setups to modernised architectures.

question.situation: A core data centre router running Cisco IOS is experiencing intermittent performance degradation during peak hours. The business has recently added several cloud-connected services, and you suspect the current bandwidth and hardware limits are being exceeded.
question.task: How do you address this performance bottleneck to ensure long-term network stability?

options.text: Implement immediate traffic-shaping and Quality of Service (QoS) policies on the Cisco IOS devices to prioritise critical business traffic while gathering usage data.
Initiate a comprehensive capacity planning exercise to model future traffic growth and justify a budget request for hardware upgrades.
Deploy a temporary load-balancing protocol configuration to distribute traffic across alternative paths while investigating the root cause.
Work with cloud providers to temporarily throttle non-essential cloud sync services during peak hours to protect local network performance.

hints: Think about the difference between immediate tactical mitigation and long-term strategic planning.
Consider how configuration changes on existing Cisco hardware can buy time before major capital expenditure is approved.

what_worked_well: Applying QoS on Cisco IOS provides immediate relief to critical services without requiring new hardware purchases.
trade_offs: This is a tactical fix that does not solve the underlying capacity deficit if overall traffic continues to grow.
areas_to_consider: Monitor the impact of QoS policies to ensure non-critical but necessary services are not completely starved of bandwidth.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Proficiency in configuring Cisco IOS commands is essential for managing traffic flow and device performance.

what_worked_well: Capacity planning provides a data-driven justification for long-term infrastructure investment, preventing future bottlenecks.
trade_offs: Gathering and analysing data takes time, leaving users to deal with performance issues in the short term.
areas_to_consider: Look for quick wins or temporary workarounds to keep the business running smoothly while the planning phase completes.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Predicting network demands ensures the architecture remains scalable as the business adopts more cloud services.

what_worked_well: Using load-balancing protocols utilises existing redundant paths, improving immediate availability and spreading the traffic load.
trade_offs: This increases configuration complexity and may introduce routing asymmetry if not carefully managed.
areas_to_consider: Verify that all alternative paths have the security controls required for production traffic.

skill_to_explore.skill: Cisco Systems Gateway Load Balancing Protocol GLBP
skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding load-balancing options helps design resilient path redundancy in multi-homed environments.

what_worked_well: Throttling non-essential cloud services directly reduces peak demand on the network without changing local configurations.
trade_offs: This requires coordination with external providers or cloud teams and might delay background business processes.
areas_to_consider: Define clearly what constitutes 'non-essential' traffic in collaboration with business stakeholders.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding how cloud traffic profiles impact local infrastructure is key to modern network capacity management.

question.situation: You are designing a highly available network architecture for a new regional office. The business cannot tolerate any internet downtime, but the budget is constrained. You need to decide on the redundancy protocols and risk mitigation strategies.
question.task: What is your preferred approach to balancing high availability with budget limitations?

options.text: Implement Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) across dual mid-range routers to provide automatic failover without proprietary licensing costs.
Conduct a formal risk assessment to present to stakeholders, highlighting the financial impact of downtime to secure additional budget for fully redundant lines.
Configure a single high-end router with redundant power supplies and modular cards, reducing initial hardware costs while maintaining internal hardware resilience.
Set up an automated monitoring system to alert the network team of failures immediately, relying on rapid manual intervention rather than automated failover.

hints: Consider how open standards like VRRP can deliver high availability without locking the organisation into expensive vendor licences.
Think about how a risk assessment can translate technical downtime into business-understandable financial terms.

what_worked_well: Using VRRP provides a cost-effective, multi-vendor standard for router redundancy, ensuring high availability at the gateway.
trade_offs: While VRRP handles router failure, it does not inherently protect against a complete WAN link failure unless paired with dynamic routing.
areas_to_consider: Ensure that both routers have consistent configuration management to prevent mismatch issues during a failover event.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Mastering open redundancy protocols allows you to design high-availability networks within tight budget constraints.

what_worked_well: A formal risk assessment empowers business leaders to make informed, value-based decisions regarding the cost of downtime versus redundancy.
trade_offs: This approach can delay the design phase while waiting for business decisions and budget approvals.
areas_to_consider: Prepare a baseline design that fits the current budget while waiting for the outcome of the risk assessment.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Aligning technical risks with financial impacts is a key skill for senior network architects presenting to stakeholders.

what_worked_well: A single high-end router simplifies configuration and management while protecting against common hardware component failures.
trade_offs: The router itself remains a single point of failure; a total chassis failure or a corrupt software update will cause complete downtime.
areas_to_consider: Evaluate the lead time for a replacement chassis under your vendor support contract in case of a catastrophic failure.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Evaluating single points of failure helps you communicate realistic uptime expectations to the business.

what_worked_well: Relying on monitoring and manual intervention keeps hardware costs low and avoids complex failover configurations.
trade_offs: Manual recovery will always result in a longer recovery time objective (RTO) compared to automated protocols.
areas_to_consider: Confirm that the network support team is staffed 24/7 to respond to critical alerts within the required business timelines.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Familiarity with robust network monitoring tools is essential for maintaining visibility when automated redundancy is limited.

question.situation: Following a major network expansion, the engineering team is struggling to maintain consistent configurations across multiple sites. The lack of standardisation is leading to configuration drift and minor service disruptions.
question.task: How do you address this configuration drift to ensure network consistency and reliability?

options.text: Establish a centralised repository using Git to version-control all network configurations and track changes systematically.
Create comprehensive, standardised network documentation and configuration templates that engineers must manually follow for every change.
Conduct regular capacity planning reviews to identify which sites are experiencing the most drift and prioritise remediation there.
Implement a network monitoring tool to automatically alert the team whenever a configuration deviates from the established baseline.

hints: Think about how modern Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles can be applied to traditional network configuration management.
Consider the role of clear, accessible documentation in establishing a 'single source of truth' for the engineering team.

what_worked_well: Using Git introduces version control, audit trails, and collaborative peer reviews to network configuration management.
trade_offs: This requires a cultural shift and upskilling for engineers who are not familiar with software development workflows.
areas_to_consider: Provide clear training and start with simple templates to ease the team's transition to Git-based workflows.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Git is increasingly used in modern NetDevOps to manage configurations as code, ensuring consistency across environments.

what_worked_well: Clear, standardized documentation provides an immediate, accessible reference point and establishes clear operational standards.
trade_offs: Manual templates are prone to human error and can quickly become outdated if the documentation is not actively maintained.
areas_to_consider: Establish a regular review cycle to keep documentation aligned with live network changes.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Accurate documentation is the foundation of any standardisation effort and is vital for troubleshooting.

what_worked_well: Focusing on high-impact sites ensures that resources are directed where configuration drift is causing the most operational risk.
trade_offs: This is a reactive approach that does not stop drift from occurring at smaller, unmonitored sites.
areas_to_consider: Use capacity planning data to identify if configuration drift is actually a symptom of sites outgrowing their original design.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding site growth helps you design configurations that accommodate expansion without requiring ad-hoc changes.

what_worked_well: Automated monitoring provides real-time visibility into unauthorized changes, allowing for rapid remediation.
trade_offs: Alerting alone does not prevent the drift from happening in the first place, and can lead to alert fatigue.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you define clear baselines so the monitoring tool only flags genuine, unauthorized deviations.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Familiarity with enterprise-grade network management suites helps in automating compliance and monitoring drift.

question.situation: You are designing a secure WAN connection for a new regional office. The business requires high-performance traffic routing for real-time applications alongside robust encryption for sensitive financial data. The existing network infrastructure is a mix of legacy and modern systems.
question.task: How do you approach balancing the performance benefits of MPLS with the security requirements of IPSEC?

options.text: Implement IPSEC over MPLS (DMVPN) to secure all traffic end-to-end, accepting the routing overhead.
Segment the traffic, routing real-time data over a standard MPLS path and sensitive financial data over a dedicated IPSEC tunnel.
Deploy MPLS for primary transport and configure IPSEC as a failover VPN path over the public internet.
Use MPLS with native provider-managed security controls, avoiding IPSEC encryption to maximise throughput.

hints: Consider how encryption overhead affects real-time traffic performance.

what_worked_well: Provides robust, end-to-end encryption across the entire private network path.
trade_offs: Increases packet overhead and processing latency due to double encapsulation.
areas_to_consider: Consider whether all traffic requires this level of encryption, as it may impact real-time voice and video performance.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding IPSEC encapsulation overhead is crucial when designing high-performance secure networks.

what_worked_well: Optimises performance for latency-sensitive traffic while securing critical financial data.
trade_offs: Increases configuration complexity by requiring separate routing policies and paths.
areas_to_consider: Ensure that the unencrypted MPLS path complies with your organisation's data privacy policies for non-financial traffic.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Traffic engineering in MPLS allows for granular routing decisions based on application requirements.

what_worked_well: Ensures high availability and business continuity at a lower cost by using the public internet as backup.
trade_offs: Failover performance may be inconsistent due to the unpredictable nature of public internet routing.
areas_to_consider: Test the failover convergence times to ensure they meet the business's recovery time objectives.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: IPSEC VPNs are standard for securing backup paths over untrusted public networks.

what_worked_well: Maximises throughput and reduces the administrative burden on your internal network team.
trade_offs: Relies entirely on the service provider's security controls, reducing direct visibility and compliance oversight.
areas_to_consider: Review the provider's service level agreements and security audits to ensure they align with internal standards.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Evaluating provider-managed MPLS security features is key to balancing operational effort with risk management.

question.situation: Your organisation is preparing for a major digital expansion that will double traffic to the core data centre over the next year. The existing firewall infrastructure is stable but operating near its resource limits during peak hours.
question.task: How do you approach planning the firewall upgrades to ensure security and performance are maintained during this growth?

options.text: Conduct a detailed capacity planning exercise using historical traffic trends to project future firewall CPU and memory needs before purchasing hardware.
Deploy a high-availability cluster of new, mid-range firewalls immediately to distribute the load and provide redundancy.
Implement strict firewall policy clean-up and rule optimisation to free up resource capacity on the existing hardware.
Transition to a cloud-based firewall-as-a-service (FWaaS) model to leverage on-demand scalability and reduce physical hardware dependencies.

hints: Think about the balance between proactive planning and immediate performance relief.

what_worked_well: Ensures investment decisions are backed by data, preventing over-provisioning or under-provisioning.
trade_offs: Delays the implementation of upgrades while data is collected and analysed.
areas_to_consider: Consider whether current growth trends might accelerate unexpectedly during the planning phase.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Accurate capacity planning helps align infrastructure spend with actual business growth trajectories.

what_worked_well: Provides immediate redundancy and distributes the traffic load to prevent bottlenecks.
trade_offs: Requires significant upfront capital expenditure and increases management complexity.
areas_to_consider: Evaluate if the mid-range firewalls can handle long-term growth beyond the one-year projection.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding clustering and high-availability configurations is vital for maintaining continuous security services.

what_worked_well: Improves firewall performance and security posture without requiring additional hardware budget.
trade_offs: May only provide a short-term performance boost if traffic growth is highly aggressive.
areas_to_consider: Identify obsolete or redundant rules that can be safely removed without disrupting active services.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Regular policy audit and optimisation are essential practices for maintaining efficient firewall operations.

what_worked_well: Offers rapid scalability and reduces the physical maintenance burden on the data centre team.
trade_offs: Introduces ongoing operational costs and potential latency for on-premises traffic.
areas_to_consider: Assess the compatibility of your existing security policies with the cloud provider's feature set.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Transitioning to cloud services requires a shift from hardware capacity planning to cost and bandwidth forecasting.

question.situation: The organisation is migrating its core services to a hybrid cloud environment. The legacy DNS infrastructure is currently hosted on-premises and managed manually, which is causing delays in provisioning new cloud resources and updating records.
question.task: How do you approach redesigning the DNS architecture to support this hybrid cloud transition?

options.text: Integrate cloud-native DNS services with your on-premises DNS using conditional forwarders to resolve names across both environments.
Deploy a centralised, automated DNS management platform across both on-premises and cloud networks to unify administration.
Keep the DNS infrastructure entirely on-premises, upgrading the hardware to handle the increased query load from the cloud.
Migrate all DNS zones completely to a public cloud DNS provider, decommissioning the on-premises DNS servers entirely.

hints: Reflect on how centralised management impacts operational efficiency during cloud migration.

what_worked_well: Maintains control over on-premises records while leveraging cloud-native capabilities for cloud resources.
trade_offs: Requires careful configuration of forwarders to avoid resolution latency or routing loops.
areas_to_consider: Ensure that security policies are consistent across both the on-premises and cloud DNS environments.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Configuring hybrid DNS resolution is fundamental to seamless resource access in cloud migrations.

what_worked_well: Provides a single pane of glass for administration, reducing manual errors and streamlining updates.
trade_offs: Involves higher software costs and requires training for the network team on the new platform.
areas_to_consider: Plan the migration phases carefully to avoid service disruption during the transition to the new platform.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Designing centralised management systems is key to scaling modern network services efficiently.

what_worked_well: Minimises changes to a critical service, leveraging existing team expertise and security models.
trade_offs: Does not resolve the manual provisioning bottlenecks for dynamic cloud resources.
areas_to_consider: Look into automation tools or APIs that can interface with your on-premises servers to speed up updates.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding the limitations of traditional DNS architectures helps in identifying when to modernise.

what_worked_well: Eliminates on-premises hardware maintenance and offers high global availability and scalability.
trade_offs: Creates a dependency on external cloud providers for internal on-premises name resolution.
areas_to_consider: Verify how on-premises clients will access the cloud DNS if the primary internet connection is lost.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Evaluating dependency risks is a core component of resilient network architecture design.

question.situation: Your company is expanding its corporate WAN by adding several new branch offices. The current network uses a static routing configuration, which is becoming increasingly difficult to manage and prone to configuration errors as the network grows.
question.task: How do you plan to transition the WAN routing architecture to a dynamic routing model?

options.text: Implement OSPF across all branches, configuring a single backbone area to simplify the initial deployment and routing logic.
Design a multi-area OSPF hierarchy to isolate routing updates and limit the impact of link failures across the WAN.
Deploy a hybrid model, keeping static routes at the smaller branch offices and running OSPF only within the core data centres.
Use a software-defined WAN (SD-WAN) overlay to manage routing dynamically, abstracting the underlying OSPF or static configurations.

hints: Consider the trade-offs between configuration simplicity and long-term network scalability.

what_worked_well: Simplifies the routing configuration and makes the initial transition from static routing easier to manage.
trade_offs: May lead to performance issues as the network grows, as every router must maintain the full link-state database.
areas_to_consider: Monitor router CPU and memory usage to determine when the network might need to be split into multiple areas.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding single-area OSPF limitations is essential for planning future network scalability.

what_worked_well: Optimises router resources and limits the propagation of routing updates, improving overall network stability.
trade_offs: Increases the complexity of the initial design and requires careful planning of area boundaries.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the team is comfortable with multi-area troubleshooting and area border router configurations.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Designing multi-area OSPF hierarchies is key to building stable, enterprise-scale routed networks.

what_worked_well: Reduces the configuration overhead on smaller branch routers while introducing dynamic routing where it is most needed.
trade_offs: Requires manual intervention whenever branch subnets change, maintaining some operational overhead.
areas_to_consider: Establish clear documentation for route redistribution between the static and dynamic environments.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Balancing static and dynamic routing is a common tactical approach in WAN management.

what_worked_well: Provides centralised control and dynamic path selection based on real-time link performance.
trade_offs: Introduces significant new technology layers and potentially higher licensing costs.
areas_to_consider: Evaluate how the SD-WAN overlay will integrate with your existing legacy core network routing protocols.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: SD-WAN technologies are transforming modern WAN architecture by abstracting traditional routing complexities.

question.situation: You are returning to network support and have been asked to help standardise the secure remote access protocols for a newly hybrid workforce. The team is currently using a mix of legacy tools, including Symantec pcAnywhere, alongside modern VPNs. Some users are reporting that their home antivirus software is flagging these legacy remote connections as suspicious, causing support tickets to spike.
question.task: How do you approach resolving the conflict between the remote control tools and the antivirus alerts while ensuring secure access?

options.text: Temporarily whitelist the legacy remote control tools in the antivirus settings across all managed endpoints to immediately reduce ticket volume while a long-term strategy is developed.

Initiate a rapid audit of all remote control software in use, proposing an immediate migration to a single, modern secure remote access solution that integrates natively with current antivirus suites.
Set up a dedicated support queue to guide users through manually adding exclusions in their local antivirus, using this interaction to gather data on which legacy tools are most critical.
Collaborate with the security team to configure strict network-level access controls, isolating the traffic from legacy remote control tools while keeping antivirus protections fully active.

what_worked_well: This approach quickly resolves user disruption by stopping the immediate antivirus alerts, allowing business operations to continue without delay.
trade_offs: While it reduces support ticket volume immediately, it temporarily lowers the security posture by allowing potentially unverified legacy tools to run without local scrutiny.
areas_to_consider: Consider setting a strict expiry date on these temporary exclusions to ensure they do not become permanent security vulnerabilities.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding how antivirus software interacts with legacy remote administration tools is essential for maintaining endpoint security without blocking legitimate work.

what_worked_well: This addresses the root cause of the issue by planning a transition away from legacy tools to a modern, secure, and fully supported remote access standard.
trade_offs: An immediate migration requires significant planning, testing, and change management, which may delay the resolution of current user issues.
areas_to_consider: Consider how to support users who rely heavily on specific features of legacy tools during the transition period.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Evaluating and standardising modern remote control solutions ensures secure and efficient support capabilities across a hybrid workforce.

what_worked_well: This allows you to gather detailed, real-world data on which legacy tools are actually needed, ensuring future decisions are based on accurate usage patterns.
trade_offs: It increases the workload on the support team in the short term and relies on users manually configuring local settings, which can lead to inconsistencies.
areas_to_consider: Consider creating clear, step-by-step documentation to help users perform these configurations safely and minimise support overhead.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Managing local antivirus exclusions requires a clear understanding of security policies to prevent users from accidentally exposing systems to threats.

what_worked_well: This maintains a strong security posture by keeping local antivirus protections active while using network-level controls to contain any risks from legacy tools.
trade_offs: Configuring complex network-level isolation can be time-consuming and may introduce additional network management overhead for the support team.
areas_to_consider: Consider how these network-level controls will affect users working from different remote locations with varying network setups.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Securing remote control traffic at the network level is a key strategy for mitigating the risks associated with legacy software.

question.situation: A regional office is experiencing severe network latency during peak hours, affecting real-time database queries. The network currently uses end-to-end encryption for all internal traffic. The local team suggests disabling encryption for non-sensitive database traffic to reduce packet overhead, while others suggest implementing traffic shapers to prioritise database queries over general web browsing.
question.task: How do you approach balancing the need for network performance with maintaining robust data security?

options.text: Implement traffic shapers to prioritise critical database traffic, keeping the existing end-to-end encryption fully active to protect data integrity.
Temporarily disable encryption on non-sensitive database segments to evaluate the performance improvement, while keeping traffic shaping as a secondary option.
Conduct a comprehensive traffic analysis to identify non-business bandwidth consumers, restricting general web browsing before adjusting encryption or shaping settings.
Upgrade the network hardware at the regional office to handle the encryption overhead without needing to configure traffic shapers or modify security protocols.

what_worked_well: This prioritises critical business traffic directly at the network level while ensuring that all data remains fully protected by end-to-end encryption.
trade_offs: Implementing traffic shaping policies requires careful configuration and ongoing monitoring to ensure other essential services are not starved of bandwidth.
areas_to_consider: Consider how future changes in network traffic patterns might require adjustments to your traffic shaping rules.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Using traffic shapers effectively allows network specialists to manage bandwidth distribution and maintain application performance under load.

what_worked_well: This offers a direct way to test if encryption overhead is indeed the primary cause of the latency, providing immediate performance data.
trade_offs: Disabling encryption, even on non-sensitive segments, introduces potential security risks and may violate internal compliance policies regarding data in transit.
areas_to_consider: Consider how you will define and verify which database segments are truly non-sensitive before altering encryption settings.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding the performance impact of encryption protocols helps in designing secure networks that do not compromise on speed.

what_worked_well: This addresses the root cause of network congestion by identifying and restricting non-essential bandwidth usage, potentially freeing up resources without changing technical configurations.
trade_offs: Conducting a comprehensive traffic analysis takes time, which means the database latency issue may persist while the data is being gathered and analysed.
areas_to_consider: Consider how to communicate any new bandwidth restrictions to staff to manage expectations and maintain goodwill.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Analysing traffic patterns is a prerequisite for configuring effective traffic shaping policies that align with business priorities.

what_worked_well: This resolves the performance bottleneck by increasing capacity, allowing the office to maintain both high performance and strong encryption without complex software configurations.
trade_offs: Upgrading hardware involves financial costs and procurement delays, making it a less immediate solution to the current latency issues.
areas_to_consider: Consider whether the existing hardware can be optimised through firmware updates or configuration changes before committing to a full upgrade.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Evaluating hardware capabilities in relation to encryption processing demands is key to planning scalable network infrastructure.

question.situation: During a routine review, you notice a series of unusual connection attempts on the corporate firewalls originating from an external IP address. The automated intrusion prevention system has blocked these attempts, but the pattern suggests a coordinated probe. The team is divided on whether to log this as a standard low-priority alert or escalate it to a full security incident.
question.task: How do you decide to handle this potential security threat to ensure both thoroughness and efficient resource use?

options.text: Escalate the event immediately through the formal security incident management process to ensure a dedicated security analyst reviews the firewall logs in detail.
Create a custom rule on the firewalls to block the external IP address permanently, then log the event as a closed, low-priority ticket to save team resources.
Monitor the firewall logs closely for another 48 hours to gather more evidence of a coordinated attack before deciding whether to trigger the incident response process.
Document the pattern in a weekly security report for team discussion, relying on the automated systems to continue blocking any further connection attempts in the meantime.

what_worked_well: This ensures that the potential threat is treated with high visibility and investigated thoroughly by specialists, adhering strictly to security best practices.
trade_offs: Escalating every blocked probe can overwhelm the security team with low-priority incidents, potentially distracting them from more critical threats.
areas_to_consider: Consider establishing clear thresholds for when automated blocks should trigger a formal escalation versus a standard log entry.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding incident classification helps balance thorough security investigation with efficient resource allocation.

what_worked_well: This provides an immediate, proactive defense by blocking the source of the probes at the firewall level, preventing further attempts from that specific IP.
trade_offs: Manually blocking individual IPs can lead to bloated firewall rule bases that are difficult to manage, and attackers can easily change their source IP.
areas_to_consider: Consider implementing automated threat intelligence feeds to manage IP reputation blocks dynamically rather than relying on manual rules.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Managing firewall rules effectively is crucial for maintaining network security without degrading device performance or creating administrative overhead.

what_worked_well: This allows you to gather more context and data to determine if this is an isolated event or part of a larger, more sophisticated campaign before raising an alarm.
trade_offs: Waiting 48 hours introduces a delay in response, which could expose the network if the attacker finds a vulnerability before the incident is escalated.
areas_to_consider: Consider what specific indicators or patterns during this monitoring period would trigger an immediate, early escalation.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Monitoring and trend analysis are vital components of incident detection, helping to identify complex attack patterns over time.

what_worked_well: This fosters team collaboration and shared situational awareness by bringing the pattern to a weekly discussion, while relying on existing automated defenses.
trade_offs: This passive approach relies heavily on the assumption that the automated systems will continue to block all variations of the attack in the interim.
areas_to_consider: Consider how to ensure that urgent or evolving threats are not delayed by waiting for scheduled weekly meetings.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Reviewing firewall event patterns collectively helps teams identify broader security trends and refine overall defense strategies.

question.situation: You are troubleshooting an intermittent connection issue between a UNIX-based application server and a database. The application team insists the network is dropping packets, but the network logs show no anomalies. You need to gather definitive proof of where the packets are being lost without disrupting the live production environment.
question.task: How do you approach diagnosing this connection issue to identify the root cause effectively?

options.text: Run tcpdump on the UNIX server during a scheduled low-traffic window to capture and analyse the raw network packets directly at the host level.
Use standard diagnostic tools like traceroute continuously from a test client to monitor the path and latency to the database over a 24-hour period.
Coordinate with the database administration team to restart the database network services during a maintenance window to clear any potential software-level hangs.
Set up a mirror port on the network switch to redirect traffic to an external packet analyzer, avoiding any direct command execution on the production UNIX server.

what_worked_well: Running tcpdump directly on the host provides highly accurate, detailed packet-level data, showing exactly what the server is sending and receiving.
trade_offs: Executing packet captures on a production server can consume significant CPU and memory resources, potentially impacting application performance if not carefully managed.
areas_to_consider: Consider using specific filters in your tcpdump command to capture only the relevant database traffic, minimising resource usage and file size.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Mastering tcpdump syntax and filtering options is essential for performing safe and effective packet analysis on live servers.

what_worked_well: Using traceroute is a low-risk, non-intrusive way to map the network path and identify any routing loops or persistent latency points between the systems.
trade_offs: Traceroute only shows the path and latency of ICMP or UDP probes, which may not accurately represent how the actual application database traffic is behaving.
areas_to_consider: Consider running traceroute at different times of day to see if the network path or latency changes under varying network loads.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Traceroute is a fundamental diagnostic tool for isolating network-layer path issues before diving into deeper packet analysis.

what_worked_well: This addresses the possibility of a software-level or service-level hang on the database side, which can mimic network packet loss to the application server.
trade_offs: Restarting services during a maintenance window requires coordination and causes temporary downtime, and it may only temporarily mask the issue without finding the root cause.
areas_to_consider: Consider checking the database system logs and resource utilisation before restarting to see if there are signs of service degradation.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding how to manage and monitor services on UNIX-based systems helps distinguish between network issues and host-level software faults.

what_worked_well: Using a mirror port and an external analyzer completely avoids any performance impact or risk on the production UNIX server, ensuring a safe diagnostic process.
trade_offs: Setting up port mirroring requires access to network switches and physical or virtual infrastructure to capture the mirrored traffic, which may take time to configure.
areas_to_consider: Consider whether you have the necessary network permissions and tools ready to capture and analyse the mirrored traffic effectively.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Analysing mirrored traffic often involves using tools like tcpdump or other packet analyzers to inspect the captured data offline.

question.situation: You are returning to a network support team where several legacy monitoring alerts are failing on a set of Ubuntu-based servers. The team has been manually restarting services because the original automation scripts are outdated and undocumented. You want to re-establish stable monitoring and automatic recovery.
question.task: How do you approach updating and validating the automation scripts to ensure long-term reliability?

options.text: Write a new, modular Shell script from scratch to handle service restarts, documenting each block thoroughly for the team.
Audit the existing scripts on the Ubuntu servers, patching only the broken paths and testing them in a sandbox environment.
Transition the restart logic to a standard Ubuntu cron job using simple systemd commands instead of complex scripting.
Collaborate with a senior colleague to pair-program the script updates, using this as an opportunity to align with current team standards.

hints: Consider the balance between writing clean, new code and reusing existing logic that the team might already be familiar with.
Think about how documentation and collaboration can ease your transition back into the team's technical workflow.

what_worked_well: Creating a new script ensures clean, modern, and fully documented code.
trade_offs: Writing from scratch requires more initial development and testing time than patching.
areas_to_consider: Consider how future team members will maintain this script when you are not available.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Developing robust shell scripts helps automate repetitive tasks and standardises system administration workflows.

what_worked_well: Auditing and patching existing scripts saves time and preserves previous operational logic.
trade_offs: You may inherit hidden bugs or poorly structured code from the original scripts.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the sandbox environment accurately mirrors the production Ubuntu servers to avoid unexpected failures.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding the Ubuntu environment ensures scripts interact correctly with system services and paths.

what_worked_well: Using standard systemd and cron jobs reduces the complexity of custom scripts and uses built-in OS features.
trade_offs: Simple cron jobs might lack the sophisticated error handling and logging of a dedicated script.
areas_to_consider: Verify if systemd service configurations need tuning to handle automatic restarts natively without cron.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Leveraging native Ubuntu service managers like systemd can simplify automation and improve reliability.

what_worked_well: Pair-programming fosters team alignment, knowledge sharing, and immediate feedback on current standards.
trade_offs: It requires dedicated time from two engineers, which might temporarily impact other support tasks.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you document the shared decisions so the wider team benefits from the alignment.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Collaborative scripting ensures code quality and helps integrate modern scripting practices into the team.

question.situation: Your network support team is planning to upgrade the company's Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) to handle increased traffic. The manager wants to ensure the transition causes minimal disruption to active business operations, but there is no formal plan yet.
question.task: How do you contribute to organising this upgrade to balance security improvements with operational continuity?

options.text: Draft a detailed project planning document outlining phased deployment windows, rollback procedures, and communication templates.
Focus on configuring the new IPS policy rules in a test environment first, ensuring high-priority traffic is white-listed before deployment.
Propose a direct, out-of-hours cutover during the weekend to complete the IPS upgrade quickly and minimise daytime disruption.
Set up a cross-departmental meeting to gather feedback on critical operational hours before scheduling any IPS maintenance windows.

hints: Reflect on how technical preparation and stakeholder communication both play vital roles in successful network upgrades.
Consider how structured planning can help manage risks when deploying critical security infrastructure like an IPS.

what_worked_well: Thorough planning minimises operational risks and ensures all stakeholders are aligned before the upgrade.
trade_offs: Creating extensive documentation can delay the actual technical implementation of the IPS upgrade.
areas_to_consider: Keep the plan flexible enough to adapt if unexpected technical issues arise during deployment.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Structured project planning is essential for coordinating complex network upgrades with minimal business impact.

what_worked_well: Testing policy rules first reduces the risk of blocking legitimate business traffic post-deployment.
trade_offs: Focusing solely on rules might overlook broader network routing or hardware performance issues during the cutover.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the test environment simulated traffic closely matches real-world production loads.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Mastering IPS configuration helps protect the network perimeter without disrupting essential business services.

what_worked_well: An out-of-hours cutover provides a clean window to resolve issues without impacting daily business activities.
trade_offs: Weekend work can impact personal time and may have limited support from external vendors if issues arise.
areas_to_consider: Establish clear go/no-go criteria and a rollback plan in case the upgrade cannot be completed in time.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding deployment strategies for security systems like IPS is key to managing maintenance windows effectively.

what_worked_well: Engaging with other departments builds trust and ensures maintenance windows do not clash with critical business cycles.
trade_offs: Gathering consensus from multiple departments can be time-consuming and delay scheduling.
areas_to_consider: Balance user preferences with the urgency of deploying critical security upgrades.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Stakeholder communication and scheduling are core components of successful network project planning.

question.situation: A critical security vulnerability has been announced affecting the main corporate file server. The patch is available, but applying it immediately requires a temporary offline reboot during business hours, which might disrupt several departments.
question.task: How do you manage this patch deployment to ensure security compliance while respecting business needs?

options.text: Schedule the file server patch and reboot for the standard weekend maintenance window, notifying users well in advance.
Apply the patch immediately during a scheduled short lunch break, sending an urgent broadcast email to all staff 15 minutes prior.
Coordinate with department heads to identify a 30-minute window of lowest activity during the day to perform the update.
Stage the patch on a secondary file server first to verify stability, then perform a rolling update if the infrastructure supports it.

hints: Evaluate the trade-off between the security risk of delaying a patch and the operational impact of sudden downtime.
Think about how staging updates can mitigate technical risks before applying changes to live file servers.

what_worked_well: Scheduling during the standard weekend window minimises immediate disruption to business operations.
trade_offs: Leaving a critical file server unpatched over the week extends the window of vulnerability exposure.
areas_to_consider: Assess the severity of the vulnerability to determine if delaying the patch poses an unacceptable risk.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Balancing security urgency with operational availability is a core challenge in patch management.

what_worked_well: Applying the patch immediately addresses the security risk rapidly, protecting sensitive data.
trade_offs: A 15-minute notice during lunch may still disrupt users with active sessions or ongoing critical tasks.
areas_to_consider: Consider the potential for data corruption if users are abruptly disconnected from the file server.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding the operational impact of rapid patching helps in executing emergency updates safely.

what_worked_well: Coordinating with department heads ensures the reboot happens during a genuine period of low business impact.
trade_offs: Negotiating a daytime window requires active communication and might still cause minor disruptions.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you have a quick rollback plan ready if the server fails to reboot within the 30-minute window.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Managing file server availability requires understanding user workflows and dependency mapping.

what_worked_well: Staging the patch first verifies stability and reduces the risk of unexpected downtime on the production server.
trade_offs: This approach requires redundant infrastructure and extra preparation time before securing the active server.
areas_to_consider: Verify that the staging environment accurately replicates the production file server configurations.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Testing updates in a staged environment is best practice for maintaining file server integrity.

question.situation: Users are reporting intermittent connection drops when accessing an external cloud database. The network route seems fine, but DNS resolution or packet loss is suspected. You need to diagnose the root cause efficiently.
question.task: Which diagnostic approach do you prioritise to isolate the connectivity issue?

options.text: Run continuous tcpdump captures on the external interface to analyse the exact packet exchange during a reported drop.
Use nslookup queries repeatedly from different internal clients to check for DNS resolution latency or failures.
Check the local routing tables and interface statistics on the gateway router to rule out hardware or path issues first.
Set up a temporary monitoring dashboard in your network tools to correlate user reports with overall traffic spikes.

hints: Consider whether a deep-dive packet analysis or a high-level DNS check is the most logical starting point for intermittent drops.
Reflect on how combining different network diagnostic tools helps paint a complete picture of the network path.

what_worked_well: Using tcpdump provides deep packet-level visibility to identify the exact point of connection failure.
trade_offs: Analysing large packet captures can be time-consuming and requires significant manual effort.
areas_to_consider: Use specific filters in tcpdump to avoid capturing excessive unrelated network traffic.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Tcpdump is a powerful tool for capturing and analysing raw network traffic to diagnose complex connectivity issues.

what_worked_well: Nslookup is a quick, lightweight way to isolate or rule out DNS resolution issues immediately.
trade_offs: It will not identify packet loss or routing issues occurring after the DNS resolution phase.
areas_to_consider: Combine nslookup with other tools to get a complete picture of the network path.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Nslookup helps verify that domain name resolution is functioning correctly, which is a common point of failure.

what_worked_well: Checking routing tables helps rule out local gateway configuration errors early in the troubleshooting process.
trade_offs: It might miss transient, external network issues or application-level disconnects.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you compare active routes with the documented network topology to spot anomalies.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding routing tables is fundamental to diagnosing where packets are being dropped or misdirected.

what_worked_well: A monitoring dashboard provides a high-level view of traffic trends and helps correlate events over time.
trade_offs: It may not provide the granular, packet-level details needed to diagnose a specific protocol issue.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the dashboard monitors the specific interfaces and protocols used by the cloud database.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Planning monitoring strategies helps teams proactively identify and resolve network performance trends.

question.situation: You have recently returned to your role as a Computer Network Support Specialist. A critical application is experiencing intermittent connection drops. The application team suspects a network-level issue, but the initial monitoring alerts are inconclusive. You need to investigate the root cause while keeping stakeholders informed.
question.task: Choose how you will approach this investigation to identify the issue and manage the communication.

options.text: Use Wireshark to capture and analyse packet-level data during a drop, while updating the team via ServiceNow.
Log a detailed incident in ServiceNow first to engage wider infrastructure teams, then set up automated alerts.
Write a custom Bash script to ping the application endpoints continuously and log latency spikes before deep-diving.
Review the recent network change logs in ServiceNow to see if any updates coincide with the intermittent drops.

hints: Consider whether you need immediate deep-dive data or a broader view of recent changes.

what_worked_well: This approach provides deep, packet-level visibility to prove or disprove network-level issues definitively.
trade_offs: Capturing and analysing packet traces can be time-consuming and generates large amounts of data.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you have the correct span ports or taps configured to capture the relevant traffic safely.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Wireshark is essential for deep-packet analysis to diagnose complex, intermittent connectivity issues.

what_worked_well: This ensures the issue is formally tracked and leverages the collective expertise of the wider infrastructure team.
trade_offs: Engaging multiple teams early might increase administrative overhead before basic triage is complete.
areas_to_consider: Consider setting up preliminary filters so that automated alerts do not flood the team with noise.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: ServiceNow helps manage incident workflows and ensures cross-team collaboration is documented.

what_worked_well: A custom script provides quick, lightweight data on latency and uptime without heavy resource overhead.
trade_offs: Pings only test basic reachability and may miss complex application-layer or protocol-specific issues.
areas_to_consider: Verify that ICMP traffic is permitted along the network path to avoid false positives.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Bash scripting allows you to quickly automate basic network diagnostics and gather initial uptime data.

what_worked_well: Checking recent changes is an excellent first step, as many intermittent issues are triggered by recent updates.
trade_offs: This relies on all changes being accurately documented in the change management system.
areas_to_consider: Look for undocumented changes or automated updates that might not have been logged formally.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: ServiceNow is the central repository for change management records, helping correlate issues with recent modifications.

question.situation: A Linux-based server in the staging environment cannot connect to a database on a different subnet. The server administrator insists the network routing is misconfigured, but the core switch configurations appear correct. You want to diagnose where the communication is breaking down.
question.task: Select the method you would use to investigate this routing and connectivity issue.

options.text: Log into the Linux server and use the route command to inspect its local routing table and gateway configuration.
Use a port scanner from a management workstation to check if the database port is open and reachable.
Run arping from the local subnet switch to verify if the database server's MAC address is resolving correctly.
Use a remote control tool to access a Windows jump box on the same subnet and test the connection from there.

hints: Think about whether the issue is likely on the host itself or within the local network segment.

what_worked_well: This directly verifies the host's own routing configuration, which is a common source of subnet communication issues.
trade_offs: This requires access permissions to the Linux server, which may require coordination with the systems team.
areas_to_consider: Check if there are multiple network interfaces on the server that might cause asymmetric routing.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding how to read and manipulate routing tables is key to diagnosing local host communication paths.

what_worked_well: This helps determine if firewalls or security groups are blocking the specific database port across the path.
trade_offs: Port scanning can sometimes trigger security alerts or be blocked by intrusion detection systems.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you have authorization to scan the network segment to avoid false security alarms.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Port scanners help verify port-level accessibility and identify firewall blocks along the network path.

what_worked_well: This confirms local Layer 2 connectivity and rules out IP address conflicts or MAC resolution issues.
trade_offs: Arping only works within the same local broadcast domain and cannot test routing across subnets.
areas_to_consider: Keep in mind that some hosts disable response to ARP requests for security reasons.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Arping is a valuable tool for probing local network neighbours at the link layer to verify MAC resolution.

what_worked_well: This isolates the issue by testing connectivity from a known working system on the same network segment.
trade_offs: It does not directly diagnose the Linux server's configuration, which might still be the root cause.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the jump box has the same network permissions and firewall rules as the Linux server.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Using remote control tools allows you to troubleshoot from different network vantage points effectively.

question.situation: Several users report they cannot access an internal web portal by its domain name, though they can access other internal services. You suspect a DNS resolution issue is affecting connectivity, but you need to verify this before escalating to the DNS administration team.
question.task: Choose the primary diagnostic approach to confirm whether DNS resolution is the root cause.

options.text: Use the dig command to query the internal DNS servers directly and verify the domain name resolution.
Run nbtstat to check the local NetBIOS name cache and name-to-IP resolution on a user's Windows machine.
Launch WildPackets OmniPeek Network Analyzer to capture and inspect the DNS traffic from an affected client.
Test basic IP connectivity by pinging the portal's known IP address directly to bypass DNS entirely.

hints: Consider which tool provides the most direct and specific answer regarding DNS query results.

what_worked_well: This provides detailed, authoritative information directly from the DNS servers, including response codes and query times.
trade_offs: It requires familiarity with command-line syntax and interpreting detailed DNS resource records.
areas_to_consider: Test against multiple internal DNS servers to ensure there is no synchronization issue between them.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Dig is a powerful command-line tool for querying DNS name servers and troubleshooting resolution issues.

what_worked_well: This helps identify local name resolution issues specific to legacy Windows networking environments.
trade_offs: NetBIOS is less relevant for modern web portals that rely primarily on standard DNS resolution.
areas_to_consider: Check if the organization has phased out NetBIOS in favour of modern DNS standards.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding nbtstat helps troubleshoot legacy Windows name resolution and local cache issues.

what_worked_well: This allows you to see the exact packet exchange, confirming if the client is sending queries and if the server is responding.
trade_offs: Capturing and filtering packet traces takes more time than running a simple command-line query.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you filter the capture to DNS traffic (port 53) to avoid searching through unrelated network noise.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: OmniPeek provides deep packet analysis to diagnose complex protocol-level communication issues.

what_worked_well: This quickly isolates whether the issue is purely name resolution or if there is a fundamental routing or hosting problem.
trade_offs: It does not diagnose why DNS is failing, which is the primary symptom reported by the users.
areas_to_consider: Be aware that some web servers are configured to ignore ping requests, which could lead to false assumptions.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Verifying basic IP connectivity is a fundamental first step in isolating network layer issues from application layer issues.

question.situation: Your organisation is upgrading its network security posture. The security team wants to deploy an inline Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) on a critical segment, but there are concerns about potential latency and false positives disrupting production application traffic.
question.task: Decide how you will collaborate on this deployment to balance security with network performance.

options.text: Propose deploying the IPS in detection-only mode first to monitor traffic patterns and tune rules before enforcing blocks.
Use Cisco Systems Cisco Traffic Analyzer to map existing traffic baselines before the IPS is integrated.
Review the network design to identify alternative chokepoints where the IPS can be placed with minimal latency impact.
Set up a test environment mimicking the production network to evaluate the IPS performance under simulated heavy loads.

hints: Think about how to gather data on normal network behaviour before making active changes.

what_worked_well: This allows you to identify potential false positives and tune rules without risking disruption to live traffic.
trade_offs: The network remains temporarily unprotected from active exploits during the monitoring phase.
areas_to_consider: Establish a clear timeline for moving from detection-only to active prevention mode.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding IPS deployment modes is crucial for balancing security enforcement with network availability.

what_worked_well: This establishes a clear baseline of normal traffic volume and protocols, making it easier to identify anomalies and size the IPS.
trade_offs: It does not test how the IPS itself will behave or react to the traffic once deployed.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the baseline capture includes peak usage periods to accurately represent maximum load.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Traffic analysis tools help you understand network utilisation patterns to inform security appliance placement.

what_worked_well: This ensures the physical and logical placement of the device aligns with best practices and minimises single points of failure.
trade_offs: Changing the network design can be a complex process requiring extensive change approvals.
areas_to_consider: Consider high-availability configurations so that an IPS failure does not cause a network outage.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Sound network design principles ensure security appliances are integrated without introducing bottlenecks or vulnerabilities.

what_worked_well: This provides a safe, risk-free environment to stress-test the appliance and observe its behaviour under extreme conditions.
trade_offs: Building a realistic replica of the production network can be resource-intensive and time-consuming.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the simulated traffic accurately reflects the mix of protocols used in the real production environment.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Designing test environments that mirror production is key to validating performance before live deployments.

question.situation: Your team is integrating a legacy transactional database with a new real-time streaming platform. There are concerns about data consistency and how the old schema maps to event streams. You need to decide how to approach the initial design and validation phase.
question.task: Choose the approach that best aligns with your preferred way of working to ensure a robust integration.

options.text: Draft comprehensive UML sequence and class diagrams to map out the data flows and system boundaries before writing any integration code.
Set up a local MongoDB instance to prototype the event payloads and experiment with flexible schemas to see what fits best.
Build a minimal proof-of-concept using Kafka to stream live test data and debug any serialization issues as they arise in real time.
Write a PowerShell script to extract sample data from the legacy system and run offline validation checks against the proposed event structure.

what_worked_well: Provides a clear, visual representation of the system architecture before any code is written.
Helps align stakeholders and team members on the integration design.
trade_offs: Creating detailed diagrams can be time-consuming and may delay the start of actual development.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the diagrams remain updated as the implementation details inevitably change during development.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: UML helps in visualising and documenting complex system integrations, ensuring all team members share a common understanding.

what_worked_well: Allows for rapid prototyping of flexible schemas without rigid relational database constraints.
Helps understand how unstructured or semi-structured event data will look.
trade_offs: A prototype in a document store might not perfectly reflect the constraints of the legacy transactional database.
areas_to_consider: Consider how data consistency and schema validation will be enforced when migrating to the final production environment.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding document-based databases is valuable when designing flexible event payloads for modern distributed systems.

what_worked_well: Provides immediate, real-world feedback on how data streams behave under realistic conditions.
Allows you to identify serialization and latency issues early in the cycle.
trade_offs: Setting up a live streaming pipeline early on can introduce unnecessary complexity before the basic architecture is agreed.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you have a robust monitoring strategy to track message delivery and handle failures in the stream.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Kafka is an industry standard for building real-time data pipelines and streaming applications.

what_worked_well: Enables quick automation of data extraction and validation tasks without modifying the core application.
Helps identify data quality issues in the legacy system early.
trade_offs: An offline scripting approach does not test the real-time integration or streaming capabilities of the new system.
areas_to_consider: Think about how these validation scripts can be integrated into a continuous integration pipeline for ongoing checks.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: PowerShell is highly effective for automating administrative tasks, data manipulation, and environment setup.

question.situation: Your organisation is migrating a legacy suite of desktop utilities written in Microsoft Visual Basic to a modern, cloud-hosted environment. The codebase is poorly documented, and some business logic is deeply nested within old UI event handlers.
question.task: Select the strategy you would adopt to initiate this migration process effectively.

options.text: Perform a direct source code migration by using automated tools to convert the Visual Basic logic into C# classes, then refactor.
Use a decompiler on the compiled binaries to extract clean logic representations, bypassing the cluttered and poorly commented source code.
Build a parallel LAMP Stack prototype of the core features to test web-based performance and usability before committing to a final architecture.
Set up a systematic debugging environment to step through the legacy application's execution paths and document the actual runtime behaviour.

what_worked_well: Leverages automated tools to speed up the translation of legacy logic into modern language constructs.
Preserves the existing business logic structure in a modern framework.
trade_offs: Automated translation can produce unoptimised or non-idiomatic C# code that requires extensive refactoring.
areas_to_consider: Be prepared to manually review and rewrite complex event-driven logic that does not translate cleanly to web paradigms.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Migrating source code efficiently is a key skill when modernising legacy systems to run on contemporary platforms.

what_worked_well: Allows you to inspect the actual compiled logic, which is useful if the original source code is missing or corrupted.
Helps verify what is running in production.
trade_offs: Decompiled code often lacks comments, meaningful variable names, and original formatting, making it difficult to read.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you comply with licensing agreements and intellectual property policies when decompiling software.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Decompilers are valuable tools for reverse-engineering and understanding legacy binaries when source code is unavailable.

what_worked_well: Enables rapid development of a web-based prototype using a mature and widely supported technology stack.
Provides an immediate sense of how the application behaves in a browser.
trade_offs: Introducing a completely different technology stack might not align with the organisation's long-term cloud architecture goals.
areas_to_consider: Evaluate whether the team has the necessary skills to maintain and support a LAMP stack in production.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding the LAMP stack provides a solid foundation in web architecture and open-source web development.

what_worked_well: Provides deep insights into the runtime behaviour and execution paths of the legacy application.
Helps identify hidden dependencies and edge cases that static analysis might miss.
trade_offs: Stepping through a large codebase manually can be highly time-consuming and tedious.
areas_to_consider: Combine runtime debugging with automated logging to capture behaviour under various user scenarios.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Advanced debugging skills are essential for diagnosing complex issues in both legacy and modern codebases.

question.situation: During a major system update, a critical performance bottleneck is discovered in the reporting database. Several complex SQL queries are locking tables, causing transaction timeouts. The team is under pressure to deploy a fix immediately.
question.task: Choose the method you would use to address this database performance issue.

options.text: Use revision control to create an isolated hotfix branch, allowing you to safely refactor and test the SQL queries without disrupting ongoing development.
Set up an interactive debugging session to trace the execution plan of the slow queries and identify exactly where the locks are occurring.
Write a PHP script to cache the query results temporarily, reducing the direct load on the database while a permanent fix is designed.
Reorganise the database indexes and rewrite the nested SQL joins to optimise the query execution path directly in the staging environment.

what_worked_well: Ensures a safe, isolated environment for developing and testing hotfixes without affecting the main release branch.
Maintains a clear history of changes for future reference.
trade_offs: Managing merge conflicts can become complex if the main branch is changing rapidly at the same time.
areas_to_consider: Establish clear branching and merging policies within your team to streamline the hotfix deployment process.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Revision control is fundamental for collaborative software development, enabling safe and organised code management.

what_worked_well: Allows you to pinpoint the exact line of code or database call causing the performance bottleneck.
Provides real-time visibility into variable states and execution flow.
trade_offs: Debugging in a production-like environment can sometimes introduce overhead or temporarily lock resources further.
areas_to_consider: Use non-intrusive debugging techniques or profiling tools to avoid impacting active users during investigation.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Effective debugging helps developers quickly identify and resolve critical performance issues and software bugs.

what_worked_well: Provides a quick, temporary mitigation to relieve database pressure and restore system stability for users.
Buys the team time to design a more robust, permanent database fix.
trade_offs: Caching can introduce data staleness issues and does not address the root cause of the slow database queries.
areas_to_consider: Ensure you define a clear cache invalidation strategy to prevent users from seeing outdated information.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: PHP is a widely used server-side scripting language, excellent for implementing web-tier caching and middleware solutions.

what_worked_well: Addresses the root cause of the performance issue directly by optimising the database execution path.
Can lead to significant, long-term improvements in system throughput.
trade_offs: Rewriting complex queries and altering indexes carries a risk of introducing regression bugs if not thoroughly tested.
areas_to_consider: Always analyse the database execution plan before and after your changes to verify the performance gains.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Proficiency in SQL and database optimisation is crucial for ensuring application performance and scalability.

question.situation: You are tasked with upgrading an outdated internal administration portal. The current interface is cluttered, slow to render, and difficult for non-technical staff to navigate. The backend services are stable, but the frontend needs a complete overhaul.
question.task: Identify the approach you would take to modernise this portal.

options.text: Apply modern graphical user interface GUI design principles to create interactive wireframes, gathering user feedback before writing code.
Rebuild the frontend using Angular to create a responsive, single-page application that binds efficiently to the existing backend APIs.
Use a debugging tool to profile the rendering performance of the current interface and patch the specific bottlenecks.
Integrate Apache Cassandra as a caching layer to speed up data retrieval, reducing the load times without changing the frontend design.

what_worked_well: Focuses on the user experience first, ensuring the new design meets the actual needs of the administrative staff.
Reduces development waste by validating layouts early.
trade_offs: Creating detailed wireframes and gathering feedback can delay the start of the actual frontend implementation.
areas_to_consider: Ensure the designed interface is technically feasible within the constraints of the chosen frontend framework.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Good GUI design is essential for creating intuitive, efficient, and user-friendly software applications.

what_worked_well: Provides a robust, structured framework for building a highly responsive and maintainable single-page application.
Offers powerful data-binding features out of the box.
trade_offs: Angular has a steep learning curve and may introduce unnecessary complexity for simpler administrative portals.
